findings.rootCause: PackedSearchBudget.tryReserve(units) set workLimitReached=true whenever units > workLimit - workUnits (even with 990 of 1000 units left) and every gate (tryReserve/tryConsume, tryReserveMandatoryCompletion, canReserveMandatoryCompletion, canBeginMandatoryCompletion, sampleDeadline, canConsume, remainingWorkUnits) returned false/0 on that flag. One refused optional block (whole-order reservations at PackedJoinEnumerator seedDenseCorrelatedIncumbent tryReserve(order.length-1), emitScheduledFilterOrder tryReserve(factors.length), emitSelectedOrder tryReserve(reservedWorkUnits)) therefore latched the search: later smaller optional blocks, greedy seeding (optimizeGreedySeeds enters through sampleDeadline) and the mandatory-completion path whose javadoc promises it 'must not leave a parent with only a scalar or disconnected fallback' were all refused, and plan quality depended on the order in which optional blocks happened to be attempted. Secondary: PackedCascadesPlanner passed budget.workLimitReached() and budget.deadlineReached() separately into PackedPlanningResult, whose constructor requires each flag to agree with the single completionStatus; with a non-latching budget both flags can be true (refused block, then the deadline), which would throw.
findings.change: Roadmap 4.6 'non-latching budgets', status flag separated from the gate exactly as the design specifies and with the critique's three 3.8.3 items addressed. PackedSearchBudget: all work gates are arithmetic (units <= workLimit - workUnits) plus the hard limits deadline/resource/unsupported; a refused block charges nothing and only sets the workLimitReached STATUS flag (search incomplete, completionStatus INCOMPLETE_WORK_LIMIT, consumed unchanged by PackedPlanningResult/PackedPlanCache/CascadesPlanner); sampleDeadline() no longer tests the flag (critique major #2, so canBeginMandatoryCompletion and optimizeGreedySeeds stay open); new exhausted() = deadline/resource/unsupported or workUnits >= workLimit for 'no work left' loop aborts. PackedJoinEnumerator/PackedIncumbentSearch: exhausted() replaces the flag-based abort only at the audited loop-abort sites (dense search after a bounded bushy turn x2, optimizeInternedMultiword after its seed, the second sparse DPhyp traversal guard, the three contextual-recipe 'no winner' gates whose only reservations are single units, PackedIncumbentSearch continuation-combination gates x3); every 'traversal stopped without a search limit' invariant throw and the 'correlated DPhyp target was unreachable' guard keep workLimitReached() as the critique's blocker demands, so a benign refusal still yields return-false, never PackedMemoInvariantException. PackedCascadesPlanner: the legacy flags are derived from budget.completionStatus() (workLimitReached = status==INCOMPLETE_WORK_LIMIT, deadlineReached = status==INCOMPLETE_DEADLINE), critique major #3; the deterministic limit keeps precedence over the deadline. Deadline semantics unchanged (optional work refused, mandatory completion admitted). Deviation from the design: named the predicate exhausted() rather than stopped() to avoid clashing with the enumerator's local 'stopped' traversal flags; the design's e2e 'budget just below the optional seed size' test was not added because no fixture in the suite exposes such a threshold deterministically and the 17 budget-sensitive test classes (366 tests, incl. PackedAccessEnablingSeedBudgetTest and PackedSearchTest which the design flagged at risk) stay green unchanged.

findings.rootCause: QueryJoinOptimizer (develop's version verbatim after the merge) ranked join candidates cost-first with connectivity only as an equal-cost tie-break (isBetterCandidate) on both paths. Heuristic path (every store when statistics.supportsJoinEstimation() is false): selectNextTupleExpr/getTupleExprCost only penalises a disconnected candidate multiplicatively by currentHighestCost while discounting a connected one to pow(cost, unbound/nonConstant), so on a connected 5-chain with cheap endpoints (1 row -> cost 6) the disconnected endpoint beat the connected 1000-row middle (sqrt(1005) ~ 31.7): observed 'p1 . p2 X p5 . p4 . p3', 'p3 X p1 . p2 . p4 . p5', 'p1 X p5 . p2 . p3 . p4'. Pairwise path (LMDB statistics, supportsJoinEstimation true): reorderStatementPatternRun, selectBestIncomingCandidate and selectBestStartingExpr admitted any constant-bearing pattern regardless of connectivity: observed 'p1 X p5 . p2 . p4 . p3', 'p3 X p1 X p5 . p2 . p4', 'p4 X p1 . p3 . p2 . p5'; a prefix-connected component could skip its bridge ([q, p, r] for prefix {s}); the restored pre-merge test reorderJoinArgsNeverChoosesCartesianPairInsideConnectedComponent failed. The merge had dropped the pre-merge connectivity guards (connectedCandidateAvailable/hasConnectedPair) and made property paths barriers of the pairwise run, because under cost-first a pattern behind a property-path bridge jumped ahead of it (LmdbEstimateAuditHarnessTest.defaultPipelineFiltersThresholdAtItsValueProducer). The packed planner's factorHypergraph adds Cartesian edges only between different components and produced no cross product for any assignment.
findings.change: Design Option A (component-scoped connectivity, roadmap 4.4 'no cross products except between disconnected components'), which explicitly reverses the merge-time choice of develop's cost-first policy. New JoinVisitor.JoinComponentAnalysis: union-find over connectivityNames(candidate) with the already-bound prefix as one virtual node (mirrors PackedJoinEnumerator.factorHypergraph's component union); legalNext(x) = x joins the prefix directly OR no member of component(x) does (a Cartesian product with that component is unavoidable and legal at any time); legalPair(a,b) = different components OR directly connected. Applied in selectNextTupleExpr (components computed over the RANKED readyExpressions so a ready bridge exists by construction, plus an explicit fallback to cost-only ranking if the legal set is empty, e.g. a not-ready SERVICE bridge - critique major; the zero-cost VALUES shortcut is kept), reorderStatementPatternRun (added to develop's admission test, so all-variable patterns keep develop's 'admit only when connected' behaviour - open question resolved conservatively), selectBestIncomingCandidate, and selectBestStartingExpr (components over the whole run so two constant-bearing patterns bridged only by a non-candidate factor cannot start as a Cartesian pair). Cost-first ranking is preserved among legal candidates, so develop's five cost-first Cartesian fixtures and the ScopeAndPairwiseStatistics family stay green (all use genuinely disconnected components). Second step (same finding): property paths are run members again (estimatorReorderableFactor = StatementPattern | ArbitraryLengthPath | ZeroLengthPath) so a path can be the bridge; connectivity for ArbitraryLengthPath uses subject/object/context only via the new connectivityNames(), used by JoinComponentAnalysis, connectedByRealBinding and isConnectedToBoundVars (critique minor), so path-internal variables create no false bridges. LmdbEvaluationStatistics/LmdbEstimationEngine already estimate Join(SP, ArbitraryLengthPath) through LmdbPropertyPathEstimator with prefix conditioning (resolvedLeaf), which was the design's precondition. Not restored, per design: reorderJoinArgsTreatsAllVariablePatternAsSegmentFence (a separate 'fence' policy the component rule does not imply); QueryJoinOptimizerReorderSafetyTest stays as-is. Fourth merge-removed test re-checked in this resumed attempt: reorderJoinArgsTreatsAllVariablePatternAsSegmentFence was re-added verbatim from 4354ff137b^1 and run (run 20260928T062719.437716Z-28530-d4377403): it FAILS (actual [sb pB ob, sc pC oc, sa pA oa, s p o]) because its four patterns are pairwise disconnected components, so the component rule leaves them to cost-first ranking; per the task rule ('restore if they pass') and the design it was removed again and not restored. The other three removed tests are restored and green.

findings.rootCause: Red LmdbSocialMediaOptimizedQueryRegressionIT#q10BindsEveryCycleEdgeFromFiniteDomainsBeforeProbing introduced by b1's 3.8.2 canonical-digest tie-break (bisected in scratch worktrees: baseline 4354ff137b green; HEAD + PackedJoinEnumerator/PackedRelationDigest/PackedPlanMaterializer red; tree minus the 3.8.3 hunks still red; HEAD + 3.8.1/3.8.6a-c/QueryJoinOptimizer green). The tie-break is not the defect: it lets the search explore a join order that LmdbPackedCostModel misprices. The mapped Frontier V2 transition conditions its probe on the statement lineage of the prefix and does not see a binding that arrives without lineage (VALUES ?d), so SP(?c follows ?d) with subject, predicate and object all bound was priced at the [S,P] fan-out (8.7 rows per invocation, 870 rows for 100 prefix rows) and planned as a prefix scan with a residual object filter (plan 31.8K vs 73.4K).
findings.change: LmdbPackedCostModel.appendFactor path (no finite lookup available): when the appended statement pattern is fully bound (subject, predicate and object bound by constants or prefix bindings, and the context either absent or bound; an unbound context variable does not qualify) and the estimated rows exceed the invocation count, rows are capped at the invocation count (at most one matching statement per invocation per context), and the uncapped estimate is recorded as planned metric plannedFullyBoundLookupUnboundedRows for observability. The access path then describes a direct lookup (accessRows <= 1). Note: in the default graph without a dataset the same triple can occur in several named graphs, so the cap is an estimate per context, not a hard bound; it can only lower a fan-out that is structurally impossible within one context. Test support: PackedCostTestSupport.restrictedPrefixContext (lmdb test tree) builds a prefix whose relations no longer describe the bag exactly (as after a correlated FILTER), which is the q10 condition under which the finite-lookup estimators stand down.
